note: HAND-AUTHORED (#3102) from logos-contract §2a: `reify` is the partial inverse of `quote` (rs `Option<Term>`, go `(Term, bool)`, ts `Term | undefined`), so a value reifies iff it is quote(t) for some term t, and is refused otherwise. A quoted variable Tuple[Atom(0x02), Atom(name)] carries its VarId's name, and a VarId's name is UTF-8 text in every core (rs holds it as a String; the derivation wire refuses a non-UTF-8 subst key as `decode subst.var: not valid UTF-8`). So a quoted variable whose name bytes are not valid UTF-8 is outside quote's image and is refused. An atom's bytes are opaque data and are never UTF-8-checked (`atom_payload_ff_is_data`). Each row is a value as its ontos-codec v1 bytes (`value_hex`), written by hand from the codec framing: an atom is 00 uvarint(len) bytes, a tuple 01 uvarint(n) children. EXPECTED in every core: every `refused` row reifies to nothing; every `reifies` row reifies to exactly `term` ({"var": name}, {"atom_hex": bytes}, {"tuple": [terms]}), and quote(term) re-encodes to value_hex byte for byte. Each ill-formed name has a well-formed sibling in `reifies` at the same lead byte or boundary: c3 28 / c3 a9, c0 80 (an overlong NUL) / 00, ed a0 80 (a surrogate half) / ed 9f bf (U+D7FF), e2 82 (truncated) / e2 82 ac, f4 90 80 80 (past U+10FFFF) / f4 8f bf bf (U+10FFFF). reify has no refusal code of its own; on the derivation wire the same quoted variable is refused `decode subst.term: value is not a quoted ground term` (derivation_wire.json `subst_term_quoted_var_not_utf8`, with the control `subst_term_quoted_var_utf8_decodes`). Before #3102 go ACCEPTED every non-UTF-8 name as raw bytes, while rs and ts refused it. The structural rows (bare atom, unknown tag, wrong arity, wrong payload kind) pin the rest of quote's image. Each replay walks every section the file carries and fails on one it has no reader for, so a section cannot be added unreplayed. The `var_names` section (#3115, seat:caa's ruling) pins CONSTRUCTION to the same domain: a VarId's name is UTF-8 text. Each row is a name as generalized-UTF-8 (WTF-8) bytes (`name_hex`): exactly the go string; for ts, the UTF-16 string those bytes decode to when they are WTF-8 (`utf16`), and no string otherwise; for rs, a String exactly when they are UTF-8 (`in_domain`). Each core checks the row's `utf16` and `in_domain` against its own reading of the bytes. EXPECTED where a core can hold the name: the constructor accepts it iff `in_domain` (go ParseVarId, with NewVarId and Var panicking by name; ts `new VarId`, `VarId.of` and `Term.var`, throwing `VarIdError`) and refuses it BY NAME otherwise, and an accepted name round-trips through quote and reify, with quote writing exactly `name_hex`. rs cannot even build an out-of-domain name, which is capability by type (research 0030 row 19): its replay records that from_utf8 refuses the bytes.

refused.name: var_name_lone_ff
refused.note: #3102's own input: a quoted variable whose name is the byte ff, which never occurs in UTF-8.

refused.name: var_name_lead_byte_then_ascii_c3_28
refused.note: a two-byte lead c3 followed by the ASCII byte 28, not a continuation. Sibling: var_name_two_byte_c3_a9.

refused.name: var_name_overlong_nul_c0_80
refused.note: the overlong two-byte encoding of U+0000 (modified UTF-8). Sibling: var_name_nul_00.

refused.name: var_name_surrogate_half_ed_a0_80
refused.note: U+D800, a UTF-16 surrogate half encoded as three bytes (CESU-8 / WTF-8), not a scalar value. Sibling: var_name_last_before_surrogates_ed_9f_bf.

refused.name: var_name_truncated_e2_82
refused.note: a three-byte sequence cut after its first continuation byte. Sibling: var_name_three_byte_e2_82_ac.

refused.name: var_name_past_max_code_point_f4_90_80_80
refused.note: U+110000, one past the last code point. Sibling: var_name_max_code_point_f4_8f_bf_bf.

refused.name: var_name_ff_nested_in_tuple
refused.note: quote(Tuple[Atom("p"), Var(ff)]): the ill-formed name one level down refuses the whole value, not only a top-level variable. Sibling: var_x_nested_in_tuple.

refused.name: bare_atom
refused.note: the bare Atom("x"): every node of quote's image is a 2-tuple headed by a one-byte tag atom.

refused.name: empty_tuple
refused.note: Tuple[]: no tag and no payload.

refused.name: unknown_tag_03
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(03), Atom("x")]: the tags are 00 (atom), 01 (tuple) and 02 (variable) only.

refused.name: tag_two_bytes
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(02 02), Atom("x")]: a tag is exactly one byte.

refused.name: tag_empty_atom
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(), Atom("x")]: a tag is exactly one byte, never none.

refused.name: tag_is_a_tuple
refused.note: Tuple[Tuple[], Atom("x")]: a tag is an atom.

refused.name: var_three_elements
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(02), Atom("X"), Atom("Y")]: a quoted node has exactly two elements.

refused.name: var_payload_a_tuple
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(02), Tuple[]]: a quoted variable's payload is its name atom.

refused.name: atom_payload_a_tuple
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(00), Tuple[]]: a quoted atom's payload is an atom.

refused.name: tuple_payload_an_atom
refused.note: Tuple[Atom(01), Atom("x")]: a quoted tuple's payload is the tuple of its quoted children.

reifies.name: var_name_two_byte_c3_a9
reifies.note: U+00E9: the lead byte c3 with a continuation. Sibling of var_name_lead_byte_then_ascii_c3_28.

reifies.name: var_name_nul_00
reifies.note: U+0000 in its one well-formed encoding, a single 00 byte. Sibling of var_name_overlong_nul_c0_80.

reifies.name: var_name_last_before_surrogates_ed_9f_bf
reifies.note: U+D7FF, the last scalar value below the surrogates. Sibling of var_name_surrogate_half_ed_a0_80.

reifies.name: var_name_three_byte_e2_82_ac
reifies.note: U+20AC, the complete three-byte sequence. Sibling of var_name_truncated_e2_82.

reifies.name: var_name_max_code_point_f4_8f_bf_bf
reifies.note: U+10FFFF, the last code point (a surrogate pair in JSON's escape). Sibling of var_name_past_max_code_point_f4_90_80_80.

reifies.name: var_name_bom_prefixed_x
reifies.note: U+FEFF then X: well-formed, and the BOM is part of the name (§8, text is its exact bytes, #2682), so it is not the variable X.

reifies.name: atom_payload_ff_is_data
reifies.note: quote(Atom(ff)): an atom's bytes are opaque data, never UTF-8-checked, so the byte that refuses a variable's name reifies as an atom.

var_names.name: four_byte_f0_9f_98_80
var_names.note: U+1F600: a surrogate PAIR in UTF-16, one scalar value, so well-formed.

var_names.name: replacement_char_ef_bf_bd
var_names.note: U+FFFD itself is a valid name. It is the byte string ts wrote for every lone surrogate before #3115.

var_names.name: empty
var_names.note: The empty name: valid UTF-8, and the zero go VarId.

var_names.name: last_before_surrogates_ed_9f_bf
var_names.note: U+D7FF, the last scalar value below the surrogates.

var_names.name: first_after_surrogates_ee_80_80
var_names.note: U+E000, the first scalar value above the surrogates.

var_names.name: lone_high_surrogate_ed_a0_80
var_names.note: U+D800 alone. ts: the string \ud800; go: three bytes that are not UTF-8; rs: no String holds it.

var_names.name: lone_high_inside_61_ed_a0_80_62
var_names.note: a, U+D800, b: a lone surrogate inside a name.

var_names.name: low_then_high_ed_b0_80_ed_a0_80
var_names.note: U+DC00 then U+D800: a low surrogate before a high one is not a pair.

var_names.name: trailing_lone_high_58_ed_a0_80
var_names.note: X then a lone U+D800 at the end.

var_names.name: byte_ff
var_names.note: 0xff never occurs in UTF-8 or WTF-8: only a go string can hold it.

var_names.name: lead_then_ascii_c3_28
var_names.note: a two-byte lead then a non-continuation.

var_names.name: past_max_code_point_f4_90_80_80
var_names.note: U+110000, one past the last code point.

var_names.name: truncated_e2_82
var_names.note: a three-byte sequence cut after its first continuation byte.

var_names.name: pair_as_two_units_ed_a0_80_ed_b0_80
var_names.note: U+D800 then U+DC00, each as three bytes (CESU-8). WTF-8 forbids it (a pair must be the four-byte form), so ts cannot read it as U+10000; go refuses the bytes.
